name: queue_full
explanation: Tempester Voice, item 2: the SPI command queue gets a full test (the Voice OS study §10 row 3). The queue holds 256 words (write index [address], read index [address], bytes); DSI's ISR appends without a test, so a 256th pending word makes the queue look empty and drops everything. Now a word arriving on a full queue ((read - write - 1) mod 256 = 0) is dropped and the queued ones are kept; the burst and Note FX counters still advance, so a dropped word never shifts the parser. The test must not slow the SPI interrupt: the Main sends a burst, 0xD6xx, 0xFC00 and 8 Note FX words back to back, one about every 110 voice cycles (16 bits at 6.67 MHz plus its loop), and DSI's ISR already takes 88-101 of them. So the Note FX path is rewritten here with the test inline (FXFAST, fewer cycles than DSI's: same queue words, same [address] counter and end, [address] = 2 after 16 bytes); the patch-burst and command paths with their inline test are in parser_guard.s; QPUT (W6 appended unless full) serves the calibration pair of parser_guard.s (DSI's decoding, and its append site [address], are no longer reached).

edits.why: goto [address] ; Note FX mode: the rewritten path
dec.b W5,W5 ; (read - write - 1) mod 256 = 0: the queue is full
append, as the original sites did
mov [address],W6 ; byte index of the Note FX block, 0-14
mov #[address],W5 ; PSV address of the command table [address]
mov.b [W5++],W4 ; command of the low byte
mov.b [W5],W3 ; command of the high byte
bra z,[address] ; one slot only: the second word dropped
bra nc,[address] ; fewer than 16 bytes: done
Note FX mode off and [address] = 2, as DSI's [address]
